GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 3732 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 12TH AUGUST, 2025 
Organic Fisheries Cluster 
3732. Dr. Mallu Ravi: 
 
   Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to 
state:  
(a) the progress of the organic fisheries cluster launched in Sikkim; 
(b) whether similar clusters are being planned by the Government to launch in other States of 
the country; and 
(c) the status of the PM-KISAN scheme extension to include fishers in it and its impacts till date?  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
 
(SHRI GEORGE KURIAN) 
 
(a) and (b) : The Department of Fisheries, Government of India has notified Organic Fisheries 
Clusters in Soreng District of Sikkim for development of organic fisheries and aquaculture under 
PMMSY with focus on development of ecologically healthy fish farming systems. Series of 
consultative meetings and stakeholder consultations involving experts, officials, and farmers were 
conducted to align the objectives of organic fisheries cluster . A detailed gap analysis study was 
carried out to identify bottlenecks and areas requiring intervention for effective promotion of 
organic aquaculture practices. A Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the Organic Fisheries 
Cluster has been prepared and infrastructure -based interventions have been initiated in the 
district. Construction of fish tanks through convergence with  MGNREGA has alr eady been 
initiated. To ensure the systematic development and sustainability of the Organic Fisheries 
Cluster, a comprehensive three-year Strategic Action Plan has been prepared. The plan includes, 
interventions in the areas of capacity building, input sup port, certification, infrastructure creation, 
and market linkage to establish a replicable and self-sustaining organic aquaculture model in the 
State. 
 
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampadha Yojana (PMMSY) inter-alia provides adoption of a cluster-
based approach to enhance the competitiveness of the fisheries sector, facilitate economies of 
scale, generate higher incomes, accelerate the growth, expansion of fisheries and aquaculture in 
an organized manner in cluster based approach . To continue the efforts for sustainable 
development of fisheries, Department of Fisheries, Government of India notified 34 fisheries 
production and processing clusters in different States/UTs to boost fish production and improve 
livelihoods. These clusters focus on specific areas like ornamental fisheries, seaweed cultivation, 
pearl farming, Saline Water Aquaculture, Reservoir Fisheries, Wetland Fisheries, Cold water 
Fisheries, Dry Fish Cluster, Integrated fish farming, and tuna fishing. 
  
(c): The Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare , Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare informed that no proposal is under consideration  for extension of PM-KISAN scheme to 
fishers. Further, it is also informed that fishers and fish farmers having cultivable land are eligible 
as per the guidelines and can get benefits of PM-KISAN scheme.

DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES

TO BE ANSWERED ON 12THAUGUST, 2025 
Improvement in Fisheries Sector 
 
3734.    Shri Kota Srinivasa Poojary: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  be 
pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government has taken initiatives towards holistic development of 
fisheries sector in all States/UTs in the country including Karnataka; 
(b)  if so, the steps taken  by the Government to improve the fisheries sector in 
Karnataka; 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government for enhancing fish production, strengthening 
of value chain, employment generation, ensuring safety and security of fisheries and 
ensuring sustainability of the resources in Karnataka; and 
(d)  the financial assistance prov ided to Government of Karnataka towards holistic 
development of fisheries sector along with funds allocated, disbursed and utilized, year -
wise during the last five years? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
(SHRI GEORGE KURIAN) 
 
(a): The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying, Government of India has taken up several transformational initiatives for holistic 
development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in the country including in Karnataka. 
Some of the key reforms are highlighted below.   
(i) Recognizing the immense potential of the Fisheries Sector and for focused and holistic 
development of the sector with fishers and fish farmers’ welfare at the core, the 
Government of India created a separate Department of Fisheries in February, 2019 
and this was followed up by creation of a new Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry 
and Dairying in June, 2019. 
(ii) Highest ever investments in fisheries sector:  The Government of India has stepped 
up investments in fisheries and aquaculture sector  in the country . From 2015, the 
central government has approved schemes with total investments of Rs 38,572 crore 
and these include; (1) Centrally Sponsored Scheme on Blue Revolution: Integrated 
Development and Management of Fisheries implemented for a period of 5 years from 
FY 2015-16 to FY 2019-20 and this scheme mobilized an investment of Rs 5000 crore, 
(2)  Fisheries  and  Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) has been 
implemented with effect from the year 2018 -19 with a total funds size of Rs 7522.48 
crore. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana  (PMMSY) has been 
implementing with effect from the FY 2020 -21 with  an estimated investment of 
Rs.20,050 crore, (3) Central Sector Sub -scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan 
Samridhi Sah Yojana (PMMKSSY) under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY) with an investment of Rs. 6000 crore.  

(iii) Additionally, the Government of India with effect from the financial year 2018 -19 has 
extended the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility to fishers and fish famers to help them 
to meet their working capital requirements. 
 
(b) to (d): The fisheries development schemes and programmes implemented by the  
Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
Government of India primarily aimed  to address the critical gaps in fish production and 
productivity, quality, technology, post -harvest infrastructure and management, 
modernisation and strengthening of fisheries value chain, establishing a robust fisheries 
management framework, skill development and capacity building, creation of employment 
opportunities, enhancement of income of fishers, fish farmers,  welfare of fishers and to 
provide social security cover to fishers.  
During last five years, the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal 
Husbandry and Dairying has approved fisheries developmental projects of Government 
of Karnataka amounting to Rs.1058.98 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada 
Yojana (PMMSY)  covering various fisheries activities for improving the fisheries and 
aquaculture sector in the State. The major activities approved inter-alia include production 
enhancing activities like establishment of hatcheries, expansion of area for freshwater 
and brackishwater aquaculture, Biofloc Ponds, Deep Sea Fishing Vessels, Up-gradation 
of existing Fishing Vessels for export competency, stocking of fingerlings in Reservoirs, 
Cage Culture in Reservoirs, Seaweed Cultivation, Bivalve Cultivation, Ornamental Fish 
rearing and breeding, Re-circulatory Aquaculture Systems, installation of Artificial Reefs 
in the coast towards sustainability, extension support systems -Matsya Seva Kendras & 
Sagar Mitras.  
The post-harvest infrastructure approved under PMMSY also including modernization of 
existing Fishing Harbours, maintenance dredging  at the existing fishing harours/fish 
landing centres , construction of Ice Plants/Cold Storages, Fish Retail Markets, Fish 
Kiosks, fish  transportation facilities like Refrigerated Vehicles, Insulated Vehicles, Live 
fish vending centres , Motorcycle with ice boxes, Cycle with ice boxes, Three-wheelers 
with ice boxes, value added enterprise , Mobile eco -friendly fish kiosk. In addition, 
communication devices including transponders, providing boats and nets to traditional 
fishermen, safety-kits to fishers, livelihood and nutritional support to fishers during fishing 
ban/lean period, insurance coverage have also been approved to Karnataka. Further, as 
on date a total 14,933 KCC cards have been issued  to fishers and fish farmers in Karnataka 
for fisheries for meeting the short-term credit requirement of fishers and fish farmers.  
The details of central financial assistance provided by DoF, GoI under PMMSY to

MINISTRYOF PANCHAYATIRAJ
LOK SABHA

PANCHAYATIRAJ INSTITUTIONS
3735. SMT. GENIBEN NAGAJI THAKOR:
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATIRAJ be pleased to state;
a. whether the Government has implemented any special programs or schemes to
strengthen Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in Gujarat;
b. if so, the details of funds released and utilized under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj
Abhiyan (RGSA) in Gujarat during the last three years, State-wise;
c. whether any training and capacity-building programs for elected representatives and
Panchayat functionaries have been conducted in the State, if so, the details thereof,
State-wise; and
d. the steps taken to improve digital governance and transparency in the functioning of
Gram Panchayats in Gujarat?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEFOR PANCHAYATIRAJ
(PROF. S.P. SINGH BAGHEL)
(a) Panchayat is a State subject and the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) supplements and
complements the efforts of State Governments, including fund support under the schemes for
strengthening and efficient functioning of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) on a
continuous basis.
The MoPR is implementing the following schemes at present:
(i) Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA)
with the primary objective of strengthening the PRI by the way of capacity building
and training of the Elected Representatives (ERs) and the functionaries of the PRI,
and providing infrastructural support like Gram Panchayat Bhawan and computers
and peripherals;
(ii) Incentivization of Panchayats (IoP), a central component of the RGSA scheme,
to encourage a competitive spirit among PRI, under which awards, including financial

2
incentives, are given to the best-performing Panchayats in recognition of their good
work in improving service delivery and public welfare; and
(iii) Mission Mode Project on e-Panchayats (MMP-ePanchayat), a central
component of the RGSA scheme, under which various e-governance projects are
funded to promote the digitalization of Panchayats, bringing efficiency, accountability
and transparency to the functioning of PRI and contributing to their overall
transformation.
These schemes are implemented for all Rural Local Bodies (RLB) or PRI in all the
States/UTs in the country including Gujarat.
Besides, the PRI receive Central Finance Commission (CFC) Grants for various
developmental works that helps in strengthening them in various ways.
(b) The State-wise status of funds released and utilised under the RGSA scheme that includes
Gujarat is given at Annexure-I.
(c) Under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) scheme, various training
programmes for the Elected Representatives (ERs) of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) are
conducted by respective State Governments, including the State Government of Gujarat, as
well as the Central Government. These programmes are implemented through institutions
such as the State Institutes of Rural Development & Panchayati Raj (SIRD&PR), National
Institute of Rural Development & Panchayati Raj (NIRD&PR), institutes of national
importance like the Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs), and other organizations like
District Panchayat Resource Centres (DPRCs).
The objective of these trainings is to strengthen governance capabilities and leadership skills
in areas such as planning, implementation, resource mobilization, and management. In
addition, thematic workshops focusing on sectors like health, education, gender equality,
environmental protection, social security, and good governance have been conducted for PRI
members and functionaries. These initiative es aim to enhance their capacity to contribute
meaningfully toward the achievement of sustainable development goals.
The State-wise cumulative number of participants trained under RGSA scheme from 2022-23
and till date, including those from Gujarat, is given at Annexure-II.

3
(d) Under the Digital India initiative, the MoPR is implementing the MMP-ePanchayat
scheme for promoting transparency, efficiency, and accountability at the grassroots level
governance by developing and popularising various digital platforms and applications. The
eGramSwaraj application has facilitated digital planning, accounting, monitoring, and online
payments at the Panchayat level. The integration of eGramSwaraj with the Public Financial
Management System (PFMS) enables real-time payments to vendors and service providers,
ensuring seamless fund flow and reducing delays. The eGramSwaraj application has been
integrated with the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) to bring transparency to Panchayat
procurement. Further, applications like Meri Panchayat have endeavoured to bring
transparency in Panchayat Governance by making public accessible to information on planning,
activities, and progress of works in Panchayat. Similarly, Panchayat NIRNAY is an online
application aims at bringing transparency and better management in conduct of Gram Sabhas
by Panchayats. An application ‘AuditOnline’ has been developed for online audits of
Panchayat accounts and their financial management. All these digital steps/initiatives are
bringing in transparency in Gram Panchayats across the country including in Gram Panchayats
in Gujarat.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA

ACHIEVEMENT OF TARGET UNDER PMAY-G 
  
3736. Mr Pathan Yusuf: 
  
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether it is a fact that the targets set under Pradhan Matri 
Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G) have not been achieved, if so, 
the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
(b)  whether the progress of the scheme is very slow in some of the 
States, if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(c)  the action taken by the Government to improve the targets and 
achievements in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
(a) & (b): In order to achieve the target of “Housing for All” in rural 
areas, the Ministry of Rural Development is implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Awaas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) with effect from 1st April 
2016 to provide assistance to eligible rural households with an 
overall target to construct 4.95 crore pucca houses with basic 
amenities by 2029. The Union Cabinet approved the implementation 
of the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G) for 
construction of 2 crore additional rural houses during FY 2024-25 to 
2028-29. As on 04.08.2025, out of the cumulative target of 4.95 crore 
houses, 4.12 crore houses have been allotted to the States/UTs out 
of which 3.85 crore houses have been sanctioned and more than 2.82 
crore houses have been completed.  
The State/UT-wise details of the cumulative houses targeted, 
houses sanctioned and completed, as of 04.08.2025 is given in 
Annexure. 
The main challenges in implementation of scheme include the 
delay in release of Central & State Share from State Treasury to State 

Page 2 of 3 
 
Nodal Account of PMAY-G, cases of unwillingness of beneficiaries, 
permanent migration, disputed succession of deceased 
beneficiaries, delay in allotment of land to landless beneficiaries by 
the States/UTs and at times General/Assembly/Panchayat elections, 
unavailability of building materials. 
(c): The PMAY-G is monitored very closely at all levels. There is a 
special emphasis on quality and timely completion of construction. 
The Ministry is taking various steps to increase the pace of house 
sanction & completion and achievement of the targets under the 
scheme. Some of which are as under:  
i. Timely allocation of targets to the States/UTs  
ii. Launch of PMAY-G analytic Dashboard for monitoring and 
supervision of the scheme. 
iii. Micro monitoring of house sanction and completion using latest 
IT tools and technologies.  
iv. Regular review by Hon’ble Minister, Secretary and Deputy 
Director General. 
v. Focus on completion of those houses where 3rd or 2nd 
installment of funds has been release. 
vi. Separate review of States with high target. 
vii. Timely release of funds as per requirements of States/UT. 
viii. Continuous follow-up with States / UTs on providing land to 
landless beneficiaries of PMAY-G.

GOTS ORGANIC CERTIFICATE 
 
3737. SHRI CHANDUBHAI CHHAGANBHAI SHIHORA: 
 
 
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंत्री 
be pleased to state : 
 
 
(a) whether  processing of textile products, yarn/cotton/fabric with Global Organic Textile Standard 
(GOTS) enables them to export it with GOTS organic certificate;  
 
(b) whether control association are certified since 2007 for GOTS certificate and also linked with 
interlok since 2021;  
 
(c) whether Intertek testing service for GOTS organic certification is available since 2021;  
 
(d) whether some problem in Intertek GOTS, led to suspension of Intertek for 7 months and in turn, 
Intertek suspended some companies including Gujarat and other States as a consequence the farmers are 
also facing loss in the price of cotton (organic premium); and  
 
(e) whether foreign payments of all the companies are stopped/withheld as supply of organic material is 
banned and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
 
 
 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज् य मंत्री (श्री पबित्र मार्घेररटा) 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES  
 (SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA) 
 
(a) to (e): National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) is being implemented by the Department 
of Commerce and is notified under the FTDR Act for export.   Under NPOP, cotton is certified only till 
production level. Thereafter, the post production activities including ginning, proc essing etc are carried 
out under private certifications.     Global Organic Textiles Standards (GOTS) is one of the private 
certifications under which organic textiles are exported.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3739 
  ANSWERED ON 12/08/2025 
 
AADHAAR-BASED PAYMENTS SYSTEM IN MGNREGS 
  
3739. Shri Y S Avinash Reddy: 
  
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether the Government has assessed the Aadhaar-Based 
Payments System (ABPS) introduced in payment of wages under 
the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee 
Scheme (MGNREGS) from 1st January, 2024; 
(b)  whether the Government has taken note that many complaints 
are being received after the introduction of ABPS in MGNREGS 
wage payments due to a mismatch between the details of the 
job cards and their Aadhaar card details; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  the remedial steps taken by the Government to address the 
concerns of the workers? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (d): To ensure timely payment of wages to the beneficiaries 
under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee 
Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NREGS) and to address the issues arising 
due to frequent changes in bank account numbers of 
the beneficiaries and subsequent non-updation, it was decided 
to implement Aadhar Payment Bridge System (APBS). This has been 
made mandatory with effect from 1st January 2024.  
  
    APBS helps in improving the transparency and accountability 
of wage distribution under the scheme and ensure faster crediting of 
wages in the account of beneficiaries. Aadhar Authentication also 
reduces leakage and corruption and ensures that only legitimate 
beneficiaries with verified identities receive wages.  In case of failure 
in payment through APBS, an alternative route to make payment is 

Page 2 of 2 
 
available through account-based payment that is National Automated 
Clearing House. Currently, against total of 12.12 crore active workers 
Aadhaar seeding of 99.65% have already been completed. State/UTs 
are continuously being monitored by the Central Government for 
achieving 100% Aadhaar Seeding and APBS conversion in 
NREGASoft. As and when any issue is flagged by the State/UT or any 
other stakeholders, the same is resolved on priority basis. 
     
Monitoring and evaluation is a continuous process under 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(Mahatma Gandhi NREGS). The Ministry regularly reviews the 
performance of the States/UTs, including the implementation of 
APBS, through various mechanisms such as Mid-Term Review, 
Common Review Mission, Labour Budget meetings, National Level 
monitoring, virtual conference meetings and field visits. Depending 
on the need and requirements for effective implementation of the 
Scheme, review and course correction are taken up.

MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

  ANSWERED ON 12/08/2025 
 
DELAY IN DISBURSEMENT OF PMGSY FUNDS 
  
3740.  Shri Vijayakumar Alias Vijay Vasanth: 
    Shri Suresh Kumar Shetkar: 
    Shri Manickam Tagore B: 
  
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  whether the Central Government has delayed the disbursement 
of funds under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) to 
several States during the last two financial years; 
(b)  if so, the details of pending payments, State and district-wise, 
particularly in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra 
Pradesh and Kerala; 
(c)  the reasons for such delays despite work completion 
certificates submitted by States; 
(d)  the steps  taken to ensure timely financial support for ongoing 
and upcoming PMGSY projects; 
(e)  whether a significant number of PMGSY roads remain 
unconnected to major district roads or National Highways, if so, 
the details thereof; 
(f)  the number of rural habitations still lacking all-weather 
connectivity to the nearest highway network; 
(g)  the roadmap for integrating PMGSY roads with National 
Highway Development projects; and 
(h)  the steps  taken to ensure seamless rural-to-urban transport 
corridors across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) to (d): The funds to the States are released on the basis of works 
in hand, their execution capacity & performance and unspent 
balances of the previous releases available with them. Funds are 

Page 2 of 4 
 
released to the States only after compliance with Pradhan Mantri 
Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) guidelines. There is no such case where 
any State has not been disbursed funds after complying with PMGSY 
Guidelines. The details of Central Share of funds allocated/released 
and road length completed State-wise, including in Tamil 
Nadu, Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala, during last 
two years is given as Annexure.    
Due to constraints such as land availability including forest 
clearance, contracting capacity with the State, compliance with 
model code of conduct for elections, there have been delays in few 
projects in some of the States. The implementation of rural roads 
under PMGSY is regularly reviewed in various meetings such as 
Regional Review Meetings (RRMs), Performance Review Committee 
(PRC) Meetings, Pre-Empowered/Empowered Committee Meetings, 
monthly review/ periodic review with the States. In addition to this, 
special review meetings are also held by Secretary/ Additional 
Secretary/Joint Secretary of Ministry of Rural Development with Chief 
Secretaries/Principal Secretaries of the States. 
Based on the requests received from the States, the timeline for 
ongoing PMGSY II and III works has been extended to March, 2026 to 
enable completion of these projects.    
(e): As per the Programme guidelines, PMGSY covers only the Other 
District Roads, Village roads /rural roads. Major District Roads, State 
Highways and National Highways does not come under the purview 
of PMGSY, even if they happen to be in rural areas.  
(f): The Union Cabinet on 11th September, 2024 approved 
implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana - IV 
(PMGSY-IV) during FY 2024-25 to 2028-29. Under the programme, 
financial assistance is to be provided for the construction of 62,500 
Kms road for providing new connectivity to eligible 25,000 
unconnected habitations of population size 500+ in plains, 250+ in NE 
& Hill Sates/UTs, special category areas (Tribal Schedule V, 
Aspirational Districts/Blocks, Desert areas) and 100+ in Left Wing 
Extremism (LWE) affected districts as per Census 2011 and 
construction/ upgradation of bridges on the new connectivity roads. 
Total outlay of this scheme will be Rs. 70,125 crore. The PMGSY-IV 
Guidelines have been formulated and circulated to all States/ UTs 
during December, 2024. 

Page 3 of 4 
 
Under PMGSY-IV, States/UTs are identifying eligible habitations 
as per the programme guidelines. The Central Government is working 
closely with the State to facilitate submission of proposals under the 
programme. 
(g)  & (h): PMGSY-III was launched in 2019 for consolidation of 
1,25,000 Km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting 
habitations, inter-alia, to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), 
Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals. The program will focus on 
upgradation of existing Through Routes and Major Rural Links based 
on priority giving importance to critical facilities like the rural 
markets and education & health facilities. However, new 
construction may be allowed only as a part of upgradation project to 
connect Gramin Agricultural Markets(GrAMs)/warehouses, 
Government hospitals and Educational Institutions, in case they are 
not connected already with a metalled road or require strengthening 
and widening of existing roads. 
Under PMGSY III, the utility value of candidate roads was high 
if the road was connecting to important routes such as National 
Highways/ State Highways. Several roads, which are joining National 
Highways/ State Highways, have been upgraded under the 
programme.  
The Government has implemented several measures to enhance 
the effectiveness and reach of PMGSY roads. These steps include: 
i. Planning through the use of Geographic Information System 
(GIS) on PM Gati Shakti. 
ii. Prioritizing all-weather connectivity to unconnected 
habitations, especially in remote and hilly areas. 
iii. Adoption of new construction technologies and materials to 
improve road durability and reduce maintenance 
costs.  Capacity building has been undertaken through 
workshops and seminars in order to disseminate best practices 
and new technologies. 
iv. Special focus on Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected districts 
to promote inclusive development. 
v. Incentivizing States for maintenance of PMGSY roads during 
their entire design life.   
vi. Intensive monitoring through IT tools.  
vii. Dedicated three tier quality monitoring mechanism set up to 
ensure adherence to standards.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3743 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 12th AUGUST, 2025 
 
Digitization of Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra 
 
3743. Shri Tatkare Sunil Dattatrey:  
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) digitized so far 
in the country, State-wise and district-wise in the State of Maharashtra including Raigad Lok 
Sabha Constituency; 
(b) the infrastructure and software solutions provided to PACS in Maharashtra as part of the 
digitization drive; 
(c) whether the Government is conducting training of cooperative members in rural areas for 
efficient digital operations, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has faced any challenges during digitization in tribal areas like 
Raigad and if so, the details thereof along with the steps taken to address them; and 
(e) the role of digitized cooperatives in enhancing access to credit and services for small 
farmers and SHGs. 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a): The Government has launched the Central Sponsored Project for Computerization of 
PACS, in 2022. Government of India initially approved 63,000 PACS under Project of 
Computerization of functional PACS with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore which has 
now been increased up to 2925.39 Crore covering 73,492 PACS which entails bringing all the 
functional PACS onto an ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based common national 
software, linking them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District 
Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). The state-wise details are at Annexure- ‘A’. 
 
Further, In Maharashtra, the total sanctioned PACS under this project are 12000. The district-
wise details are at Annexure- ‘B’. including Raigad District which has 122 PACS. All 122 
PACS have been provided hardware and have been onboarded on ERP Software. 
 
(b): Under Computerization of PACS Project, hardware comprising Desktop PC with web 
camera, UPS, VPN, Biometric device, printer have been made available for all the sanctioned 
12,000 PACS. The software solution under this project is ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) 
based common national software. 
 

In Maharashtra, the ERP software is available in English and Marathi languages which 
provides separate modules for various activities of the PACS. 
 
(c): Yes, Sir. The Government is conducting training of cooperative members in rural areas for 
efficient digital operations . The details of training and hand-holding provided to the PACS 
members under this Project are at Annexure-‘C’. In Maharashtra, a host of training programs 
have been organized for various stakeholders under the project, the details of which are as 
under:- 
▪ A Basic Orientation Training Programme for Master Trainers was conducted 
from 18-20 August 2023, with 224 master trainers identified from StCB, DCCBs, and 
SI. 
▪ A training programme for 148 Core Master Trainers (CMTs) was conducted in 
May and June 2024. 
▪ Additionally, a Training of Master Trainers programme was conducted in all 
districts for 48 Master Trainers from both DCCBs and SI during July and August 2024. 
 
(d): No, Sir. All necessary facilities for the computerization of PACS in Raigad district have 
been provided through the District Central Cooperative Bank(DCCB) without any challenge. 
All 122 sanctioned PACS have now been onboarded to ePACS with the help of DCCB. 
 
(e): The digitization of PACS plays a critical role in enhancing access to credit and allied 
services for small and marginal farmers, as well as Self Help Groups (SHGs), in the following 
ways: 
• Improved transparency and accountability  in credit disbursal and repayment, 
reducing leakages and delays. 
• Faster processing  of loan applications and service requests through integrated 
software platforms. 
• Real-time data availability , enabling better credit planning and inclusion of 
underserved sections. 
• Direct benefit transfer (DBT) integration, ensuring timely credit of subsidies and 
schemes to beneficiaries. 
• Support for financial inclusion , enabling PACS to offer basic banking services 
and act as business correspondents of banks. 
• It is envisaged that PACS when transitioned to ePACS may be more efficient due 
to convenience in accounting, MIS and operations, which will enable them to 
service their members, be these Self Help Group  (SHGs) and Farmers Producer 
Organization ( FPOs) or individuals, in a better way. This support may enable 
PACS to take up additional activities; viz CSC, Fertiliser Units, Soil Health 
Testing, etc., which helps them in dispensing better services.  Digitized 
cooperatives play a vital role in enhancing access to credit and services for small 
farmers and Self-Help Groups (SHGs). 
 
****

BENEFICIARIES UNDER IGNDPS 
  
3745. Shri Asaduddin Owaisi: 
   Shri Bastipati Nagaraju: 
  
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the number of beneficiaries currently covered under the Indira 
Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS), 
specifically for persons with disabilities and further categorized 
by type of disability, State and UT-wise; 
(b)  the eligibility criteria for availing benefits under the said scheme 
and the rationale for limiting pension coverage to only those 
with 80% or more disability; 
(c)  the amount of pension (in absolute figures) currently provided to 
the persons with disabilities under IGNDPS; 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to increase the Central 
Government’s contribution to the disability pension component 
under the scheme; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a): Under Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme 
(IGNDPS), overall State/UT-wise cap of number of beneficiaries is 
8.33 lakh, State/UT-wise details of which is given in Annexure.The 
beneficiaries belonging to severe/ multiple disabilities from BPL 
category are covered for availing assistance under the scheme. 
Under the State/UT cap, there is no categorization or ceiling 
prescribed based on type of disability. However, as per scheme 
guidelines, it is the responsibility of the State/UT concerned to 
proactively identify the most deserving beneficiary among the 
disabled persons, as per the prescribed eligibility criteria. 

Page 2 of 3 
 
(b): IGNDPS introduced in 2009 under National Social Assistance 
Programme (NSAP) does not have universal coverage.  Out of the 
disabled persons, in terms of scheme guidelines, the most vulnerable 
category of persons with severe or multiple disability belonging to 
BPL category in the age of 18 years and above are eligible for 
assistance under IGNDPS. As per guidelines, in view of the limitation 
of fund available, if there are more deserving beneficiaries, the 
State/UT has the option to give them pension from its own resources. 
(c): The central assistance under the IGNDPS is ₹300/- per month 
per beneficiary from 18 to 79 years of age and ₹ 500/- per month per 
beneficiary from 80 years onwards. The States/UTs are encouraged 
to provide top-up amount of at least an equivalent amount to the 
assistance provided by the Central Government so that the 
beneficiaries could get a decent level of assistance. At present, the 
States/UTs are adding top-up amount ranging from ₹200/-  to ₹ 5700/- 
per month per beneficiary under disability pension scheme. 
(d) & (e): While considering the continuation of NSAP schemes for 
the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-26), the revision in 
beneficiary coverage and rate of assistance under the schemes was 
considered by the Government. However, considering the available 
financial space, the Government has approved continuation of NSAP 
schemes in its present form.

(a) whether the drone mapping coverage under the Survey of Villages and mapping with
improvised technology in village areas (SV AMITV A)scheme has contributed to a precise
distribution of property cards, and if so, the data thereof;
(b) whether the SV AMITV Ascheme has contributed to increased improvements in rural
governance and enhanced the implementation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs),
and if so, the data thereof;
(c) whether the preparation and distribution of these property cards have led to the empowerment
of rural women with legal property ownership and if so, the data thereof;
(d) whether the scheme significantly reduced property disputes and if so, the data thereof
particularly State-wise including Gujarat; and
(e) the details on the manner in which the scheme has led to better access to institutional credit
while empowering rural citizens?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEFOR PANCHAYATIRAJ
(PROF. S. P. SINGH BAGHEL)
(a) Yes sir, drone mapping coverage SV AMITV Ascheme has contributed to a precise
distribution of property cards. As on 6th August 2025, drone survey has been completed in 3.26

2
lakh villages out of the targeted 3.44 lakh villages; 2.63 Crore property cards have been prepared

PM-AASHA 
3748. SHRI DAMODAR AGRAWAL: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष और ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the manner in which the integrated implementation of Price Support Scheme and 
Price Stabilization Fund under Pradhan Mantri Annadata flag Sanrakshan Abhiyan help in 
providing remunerative prices to farmers and to make available product affordable prices to 
consumers;  
(b) manner in which the Government provide support to farmers before their registration 
for assured purchase by National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India 
Limite (NAFED) and National Cooperative Consumer Federation of India Limited at 
Minimum Support Price; and   
(c) the manner in which the e-Samriddhi and e-Samukti portals of National Agricultural 
Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Limited (NAFED) and National Cooperative 
Marketing Federation of India Limited (NAFED) and National Cooperative Consumer 
Federation of India Limited make the process of registration of farmers and purchase of 
produce easy and transparent? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): The Government of India is implementing the integrated Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay 
Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) with the objective of ensuring remunerative prices to 
farmers and making essential commodities available to consumers at affordable prices. The 
scheme components are Price Support Scheme (PSS) and Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF), 
along with Price Deficit Payment Scheme (PDPS) and Market Intervention Scheme (MIS).  
PSS is operationalised on request of the concerned State/UT Governments when 
market prices of notified pulses, oilseeds, and copra fall below the notified Minimum Support 
Price (MSP) during the peak harvesting period. The primary objective of this component is 
to safeguard farmers against distress sales by ensuring procurement at MSP. Under PSS, 
procurement of eligible commodities conforming to the prescribed Fair Average Quality 
(FAQ) standards is undertaken by designated Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs) i.e. National 
Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and National 

Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF), which operate through State-level 
agencies. Procurement is carried out directly from pre-registered farmers who possess valid 
land records, thereby eliminating the role of intermediaries and ensuring that the benefits of 
MSP accrue directly to farmers. 
The Department of Consumer Affairs administers the PSF component of integrated 
PM-AASHA with an objective of protecting consumers from volatility in prices of agri-
horticultural commodities and ensure availability at affordable prices. The commodity 
procured under PSF buffer are released in a calibrated manner during low supply and lean 
season. The Government maintains the buffer stocks of major pulses such as Tur, Urad, 
Chana, Moong, Masur and onion under PSF. 
The integrated implementation of PSS and PSF under PM-AASHA ensures a 
balanced approach that supports farmers through assured procurement at MSP and 
addresses consumer interests through price stabilisation measures, contributing to both 
farmer welfare and food price stability. 
(b):  Under PM-AASHA, the Government provides support to farmers well before the 
commencement of procurement operations through CNAs, State Governments, and their 
designated agencies. To facilitate farmer participation and smooth registration, extensive 
awareness generation and publicity activities are undertaken in advance of the procurement 
season by CNAs, State Governments, and Primary Procuring Agencies through electronic 
and print media.  
(c):  To ensure transparency, efficiency, and ease of operations under the Price Support 
Scheme (PSS), NAFED and NCCF have developed dedicated digital platforms: e-Samriddhi 
and e-Samukti respectively. These portals streamline the entire procurement process, from 
farmer registration to final payment, thereby reducing manual intervention. Farmers can 
register themselves on these portals by providing basic details such as Aadhaar number, 
land records, bank account information, crop details etc. Pre-registered farmers, if willing to 
offer their stock under the scheme, can select their nearest purchase centre, thereafter, 
scheduling is done by portal for physical visit to centre on a particular date. This system 
ensures timely and direct transfer of MSP payments into farmers’ bank accounts, 
eliminating delays and intermediaries.
